title: EIT in solid-state defect centers: sector-mediated response classification
one_line: Transparency redefined as coherent cancellation in the sector-mediated response, classified by an integer suppression index nu — structurally established, experimentally unmeasurable on the platform it was built for.

authority.rule: certificates in results/certificates/ outrank prose; CLAIMS.md and NON_CLAIMS.md outrank campaign documents

claims.claim: exclusive trichotomy of the suppression index nu
the sector cut chi - chi_cut^(S), not chi_full, is the object of a no-go statement
matched-readout transparency has an identity floor Re chi = x^dag Gamma x >= 0
response-theoretic definition of EIT and its equivalent conditions
NV binary no-go and the K ~ B_perp^2 transverse-field pathway
a finite measurement window exists for a 3-mode engineered-loss chain

non_claims: N1 a measurable design rule across engineered-dissipation platforms
N2 optical NV can measure its own suppression exponent
N3 Gate B gives a measurement procedure for a superconducting device
N4 group-IV curves as quantitative predictions
N5 Gate E's 3-mode PASS as experimentally demonstrated
N6 T1 Theorem 2.1 as a result of this repository
N7 T1 Theorem 2.3(ii) as a genericity statement
N8 manuscript Fig. 4 as a quick=False figure
N9 random scans as evidence for a positivity claim
N10 absence from the Zotero library as evidence of novelty
open_questions: O1 is there any platform where nu is both large enough to matter and small enough to measure? note: every nu reported here is an ideal-cut value, the corner of the two-scale fan where the exponent is largest; the declared resource path is a second unexploited axis. see theory/NOTE_path_dependence_and_O1.md. this does not reopen non-claim N2.
O2 does the sector-cut classification have an observable signature that is not the exponent?
O3 what is the right genericity statement for T1 Theorem 2.3(ii)?
O4 can the unmatched escape route (exact zeros with x in ker Gamma) be characterized?
